newsitem.title: USA: Boeing, McDonnell Douglas in pact on strike fighter.
newsitem.headline: Boeing, McDonnell Douglas in pact on strike fighter.

text.p: Boeing Co. and McDonnell Douglas Corp., which plan to merge, said Monday they agreed to work together on a new joint fighter aircraft being developed by Boeing for the U.S. armed forces and the British navy.
The companies said in a statement that they signed a memorandum of agreement on Jan. 20 similar to one made public late last year involving commercial programmes.
Initially, the agreement will involve about 50 McDonnell Douglas engineers and managers working on Boeing's proposed version of the so-called Joint Strike Fighter, the announcement said.
Some of the McDonnell Douglas workers will temporarily relocate to Seattle to work on the programme, with the remainder working on related tasks in St. Louis, where McDonnell is based.
The specifics of their assignments will be defined as the work evolves, the companies said.
The Joint Strike Fighter is multi-service aircraft that will be used in the next century by the U.S. Air Force, Marine Corps, Navy and the British Royal Navy.
The armed forces are expected to need as many as 3,000 Joint Strike Fighters to replace several different aircraft now in service.
Boeing was awarded a $662 million contract from the Department of Defence last November to proceed with the Concept Demonstration Phase of the Joint Strike Fighter programme.

Mickey Michellich, Boeing vice president for the fighter programme, said the teaming will allow the company to take full advantage of McDonnell Douglas' experience in designing and manufacturing fighter aircraft.
"McDonnell has a proud heritage in tactical aviation and we are excited about the prospects of applying their expertise to the Boeing Joint Strike Fighter programme," Michellich said.
Boeing and McDonnell Douglas have worked together on other aerospace projects. Both are members of the team responsible for the design and construction of the international space station.
Boeing's stock lost 75 cents to $106.375 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange while McDonnell Douglas gave up $1 to $66.25 on the NYSE.
